what_its_for: Caspofungin is an antifungal medicine used to treat serious fungal infections in your body, including infections caused by Candida (yeast) or Aspergillus fungi. It is often used when other antifungal medicines have not worked or cannot be used. It may also be used to prevent fungal infections in people with weakened immune systems.
how_to_take: Caspofungin is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion directly into your vein by a nurse or doctor in a hospital or clinic setting. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home in most cases. Each infusion is slowly given over about 1 hour. Do not rush or speed up the infusion on your own.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight, the type of infection you have, and how well your liver is working. A typical starting dose for adults is 70 mg on the first day, followed by 50 mg once daily on the days after that. Children's doses are calculated based on body surface area. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose without asking your doctor first.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by a healthcare professional in a medical setting, a missed dose should be handled by your medical team. If you miss a scheduled appointment or infusion, call your doctor or clinic right away to reschedule as soon as possible. Do not try to double up on doses.
storage: Caspofungin is stored and prepared by healthcare professionals. The vials (small bottles) should be kept in a refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C) before use. Once the medicine is mixed and ready for infusion, it can be kept at room temperature for up to 24 hours or in the refrigerator for up to 48 hours. Do not freeze the prepared solution.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take before starting caspofungin. Avoid taking rifampin, certain anti-seizure medicines (like phenytoin or carbamazepine), or other medications that may interact with caspofungin without your doctor's knowledge. Avoid drinking alcohol excessively during treatment, as it can stress your liver. Do not stop treatment early just because you feel better — finish the full course your doctor prescribed.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you notice: difficulty breathing or wheezing, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, severe skin rash, hives, or itching (signs of an allergic reaction), flushing or warmth in your face during the infusion, chest tightness or fast heartbeat, yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine or pale-colored stools (signs of liver problems), unusual tiredness or weakness, or signs of low potassium such as muscle cramps or weakness.
when_it_works: Caspofungin starts working against the fungal infection right away after your first dose, but you may not feel better immediately. Improvement in symptoms often begins within a few days of starting treatment. Your doctor will monitor your progress with blood tests and other checks. It is very important to complete the full course of treatment even if you start feeling better, because stopping too soon can allow the infection to come back.
special_populations: Liver problems: If you have moderate to severe liver disease, your doctor may lower your dose because caspofungin is processed by the liver. Kidney problems: No dose change is usually needed for kidney problems alone. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Caspofungin is generally not recommended during pregnancy unless the benefit clearly outweighs the risk. Breastfeeding: It is not known if caspofungin passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Caspofungin can be used in infants, children, and teenagers, but the dose is carefully calculated by the doctor based on the child's size. Elderly patients: Older adults generally do not need a dose adjustment, but their doctor will monitor them closely.
